name: Tenstorrent Blackhole Tensix (p100a / p150a / p150b)
memory_bandwidth_basis: Vendor table states 512 GB/s for p150a/p150b with 32 GB GDDR6 at 16 GT/sec on a 256-bit bus, and 448 GB/s for the 28 GB p100a. 256-bit x 16 GT/s / 8 = 512 GB/s, so the stated figure is consistent with the bus width.
notes: Per p150 card (1 Blackhole ASIC, 120 Tensix cores, 16 SiFive x280 'big RISC-V' cores, 180 MB SRAM, 32 GB GDDR6, 300 W, PCIe 5.0 x16, 75 W idle). Only BLOCKFP8 is published as a throughput figure (664 TFLOPS); FP16, BF16 and FP32 TFLOPS are not given, so they are omitted. Note the block-float qualifier: this is BLOCKFP8 (block-scaled FP8), not plain FP8, and the two are not interchangeable for roofline work. The architectural change from Wormhole is that capacity and bandwidth roughly doubled per card (12 -> 32 GB, 288 -> 512 GB/s) while SRAM grew 108 -> 180 MB, and scale-up moved from 200G QSFP-DD to four passive 800G QSFP-DD ports. Compute-to-byte is 1297 FLOP/byte on BLOCKFP8, so Blackhole is much closer to compute-bound than Wormhole, but at 512 GB/s it is still memory-bound for batch-1 decode. GDDR6 rather than HBM is a deliberate cost choice: it puts these cards in the desktop price band (p150 ~USD 1400, p100a ~USD 999). Process node is not published. Variant differences: p100a has 28 GB / 448 GB/s / no QSFP-DD; p150b is the passively cooled rack version of the p150a.
